tom (runtime): Heads-up — seeing a 95th-percentile token latency spike on dedicated-pool eu-west-1 around 02:10-02:25 UTC. Affects chat and rerank routes.
maria (infra): Which pool id and did anything auto-scale or change GPU kernels during that window?
jean (platform): Per-route KPIs already show chat/rerank divergence, can you paste the raw metric slices?
tom (runtime): quick snippet from Prometheus for that window (sampling 02:05-02:30):
```
redwood_pool_token_latency_seconds_bucket{pool="dedicated-eu-w-1",route="chat",le="0.05"} 112
redwood_pool_token_latency_seconds_bucket{pool="dedicated-eu-w-1",route="chat",le="0.1"} 804
redwood_pool_token_latency_seconds_bucket{pool="dedicated-eu-w-1",route="chat",le="0.5"} 912
redwood_pool_token_latency_seconds_sum{pool="dedicated-eu-w-1",route="chat"} 74.2
redwood_pool_tokens_total{pool="dedicated-eu-w-1",route="chat"} 1200
```
That 95p jumped from ~0.12s to ~0.42s.
jean (platform): Thanks. I also pulled the token-level breakdown dashboard — there is a clear bimodal tail for chat routes. Link: https://grafana.internal/d/dedicated-pools/token-latency?orgId=1 (temp)
li (ml): I ran a quick profiler on a representative request sample. KV-cache hit-rate dropped sharply in the same window. Sample KV stats: `kv_cache_hit_rate=0.39 -> 0.78` before/after — which explains extra KV fetch latency into the critical path.
ops-bot: autoscaler: policy-change applied to dedicated-eu-w-1 at 2026-09-13T02:12:10Z (scale_policy: burst_enabled=false) :information_source:
maria (infra): That autoscaler change looks like it might have forced requests onto a smaller set of GPUs and changed batch shapes. Any kernel selection logs?
tom (runtime): Yes — from runtime traces we saw a fallback to the generic GEMM kernel for a subset of seq_len > 1024 when quantized kernels reported a mismatch. Trace snippet:
```
[02:11:07] model=redwood-v2-1b variant=q4_0 kernel_assigned=matmul_generic reason="quant-kernel-mismatch-seq>1024"
[02:11:07] kv_cache_lookup_latency_ms p50=1.2 p95=15.4
```
li (ml): That fallback can blow up per-token latency if it happens mid-stream; also continuous batching heuristics exposed different sequence-length grouping, so large sequences ended up alone -> smaller batch throughput.
jean (platform): Proposed dashboard changes: add panels for `kernel_selection_count{kernel=...}` by model_variant, `kv_cache_hit_rate` by route + pool, and `batch_size_distribution` heatmap per pool. Want to show noisy-neighbor_score and capacity_headroom on the dedicated pool overview.
tom (runtime): Good. For instrumentation I suggest adding a light-weight `kernel_decision` counter with labels: model, variant, seq_bucket (<=128,129-512,513-1024,>1024). Also emit `kv_cache_miss_reason` (evicted|stale|cold-start) when miss happens.
maria (infra): I'll add noisy-neighbor detection signals from the allocator: `allocation_churn`, `active_preemptions`, and `noisy_neighbor_score` computed from request variance across compute slices. I'll wire those into the pool dashboard.
jean (platform): I'll create a temp dashboard and populate those panels. Can we agree on a noise threshold? proposal: noisy_neighbor_score > 0.6 + capacity_headroom < 20% triggers annotation/alert.
li (ml): One more: correlate kernel-selection with quantization-profile used. If a model variant uses `q4_0` but runtime resorts to generic kernel, we need that mapping in dashboard to spot mismatches.
tom (runtime): Agreed. Action items: 1) instrument kernel_decision counter (me) 2) emit kv_cache_miss_reason (li) 3) add allocator signals (maria) 4) jean to temp dashboard + alert rule. I'll spin up a canary with explicit kernel pinning for the model and run through 2000 sample requests to validate.
jean (platform): Done — temporary dashboard created at https://grafana.internal/d/temp/dedicated-kernel-kv (expires in 72h). I've added panels and a noise alert (mute for 1h while we test).
tom (runtime): I'll attach a small perf trace and the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3187 — adding logs and profiling artifacts.
maria (infra): Scheduling a short maintenance window to test autoscaler rollback to previous policy at 03:00 UTC. Will follow up in this thread.
tom (runtime): Thanks — please post results. If noisy_neighbor_score correlates with the spike, we can add an autoscale safety rule to prefer even GPU distribution before bursting down. :thumbsup:
